claims.text: MnNiSi-based alloys can exhibit a large magnetocaloric effect.
Conventionally processed MnNiSi-based alloys have inferior mechanical performance, including low toughness and ductility.
A tailored aging heat treatment can induce a fine dispersion of nanoscale precipitates in the MnNiSi-based matrix.
Heating at approximately 550–600 °C for about one hour followed by rapid quenching will form nanoscale precipitates without significant coarsening.
The proposed 550–600 °C treatment lies near but below the relevant transformation threshold.
The heat treatment will produce nanoprecipitates at grain boundaries or within grains.
The nanoprecipitates will provide dispersion strengthening.
The nanoprecipitates will not substantially alter the matrix's magnetic ordering or transformation characteristics.
Nanoscale precipitates act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion and crack propagation will increase mechanical strength and toughness.
Maintaining a low precipitate volume fraction will largely preserve the primary magnetostructural transition responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
The treated material will have higher fracture toughness than the untreated as-cast material.
The treated material will have better ductility than the untreated as-cast material.
The treated material will retain an isothermal magnetic entropy change comparable to that of untreated material.
Excessive precipitation could reduce the magnetocaloric effect by altering magnetic interactions.
Excessive precipitation could adversely affect the phase transformation behavior.
